opening.phase_description: The first 10-15 moves where both sides develop pieces and fight for the center
main_goals: Control the center (e4, d4, e5, d5 squares)
Develop all pieces to active squares

principles.development: Move each piece once before moving any piece twice
principles.center_control: Control the center with pawns and pieces - it's the highway of the board
principles.king_safety: Castle early - usually within the first 10 moves
principles.piece_activity: Develop pieces to squares where they have options

common_mistakes: Moving the same piece multiple times
Bringing the queen out too early

middlegame.phase_description: The strategic battle where both sides execute their plans and create threats
main_goals: Create a concrete plan based on the position
Coordinate pieces for attack or defense

principles.planning: Every move should be part of a plan - what are you trying to achieve?
principles.piece_coordination: Pieces work together - one piece alone rarely achieves much
principles.prophylaxis: Before your move, ask: what does my opponent want to do?
principles.pawn_structure: Pawn structure determines piece placement - knights need outposts, bishops need diagonals

common_mistakes: Trading active pieces for passive ones
Creating weaknesses in your own position
key_questions: What is my worst piece and how can I improve it?
Where are the weak squares in both positions?

endgame.phase_description: The final phase with fewer pieces where technique and king activity matter most
main_goals: Activate your king - it becomes a strong piece
Coordinate pieces to support pawn promotion
Simplify when ahead, avoid trades when behind

principles.king_activity: The king is a fighting piece in the endgame - bring it to the center
principles.passed_pawns: Passed pawns must be pushed - they tie down enemy pieces
principles.rook_activity: Rooks belong behind passed pawns (yours or opponent's)
principles.opposition: In king and pawn endings, controlling the opposition is crucial

common_mistakes: Placing rooks in front of passed pawns
Trading into a losing pawn endgame
key_techniques: King and pawn vs king - the square rule
Knight vs bishop - depends on pawn structure
Same-colored bishop endings - outside passed pawns win
